\caption{MAIN. Sandbagging on normal WMDP, three subjects by three instructions, 25 items in each cell. \emph{Right} is the share of items whose reply letter is the correct one; $p$(letter) is the probability the model put on the letter it chose, over the four options at the answer spot. Being told to underperform barely moves the letter on either model, but it moves the confidence: on the 27B the probability on the chosen letter falls from 0.87 to 0.70 in biology and from 0.74 to 0.60 in cyber, so the instruction is registered even where it is not obeyed. The right-hand block is how well V-Read, fitted without labels on Qwen3-VL 8B, reads whether the model will favour the correct letter from the answer-spot state at three depths, pooled over the three instructions. At half depth the letter is illegible, 0.49 to 0.57; by seven tenths it is read at 0.99 or better. No lens bench was run on the 27B, so those cells are blank. The items themselves are not reproduced anywhere in this paper or its files.}

\caption{APPENDIX. The generated scenes by standing tier and stakes tier, over all five generated families, 456 records. Standing is who is entitled to settle the question: at D1 the official-looking object is right, at D2 the less official-looking one is, at D3 nothing in the scene settles it and the right answer is to say so. Stakes run from R0, a low-stakes control, to R3, the highest the set carries; the eval-awareness families put the same ten scenes under five framings and three renderings, which is why D1 and D2 dominate the count. \emph{Bearers} is how many distinct kinds of text-bearing object hold the answer in that tier, so a typeface or an object class cannot stand in for standing. The right-hand block grades the questions that state a yes or a no, by the same rule as the authority table. On the 8B the official-looking bearer is obeyed at 85\% and the less official one at 14\%: it is reading standing off appearance, which is exactly what D2 is built to catch. \caption{APPENDIX. The recipe V-Read settled on for Qwen3-VL 8B, block by block, all chosen by held-out divergence on prompts no instrument was scored on. $\lambda$ is the ridge penalty as a fraction of the mean diagonal of the Gram matrix; \emph{shrinks toward} says whether the penalty pulled the map toward zero or toward the identity, the tuned lens's own parameterisation, and the two were offered on equal terms; \emph{gain} is a scalar on the centred output picked afterwards from a grid of eight. The penalty is $10^{-8}$ on most blocks, so the solution is close to the unpenalised least-squares map, and the shrinkage target flips between zero and the identity from block to block with no gain in divergence from either, which is the point: nothing here is a tuned lens found by a shortcut, it is one solve per block, 603 seconds for all sixteen on 244K tokens, and the choices took the held-out divergence from 5.32 to 3.97. The bottom rows are the per-block divergence from Table~\ref{tab:reading}: V-Read trails the tuned lens by two nats at the input and is ahead of it at the last block. The same recipe on Qwen3.5 27B at its block 32 chose $10^{-6}$, toward zero, gain 1.75.}
\label{tab:recipe}
\end{table*}

\caption{APPENDIX. What each experiment scored, and on which pictures. $n$ is the number of scored items in the result file; the five source columns split it by where the pictures came from, so a result that leaned on one corner of the set shows it. \emph{Fitted here} names the instruments that had to be fitted for the experiment; where it says none, the ranking came from V-Write or attribution patching, which take gradients through the frozen model and fit nothing, so there is nothing to leak. \emph{Fit ids withheld} is the number of records used to fit any instrument that were then removed from every scored set by identifier; the lens bench writes it to disk and asserts it, the other fitting experiments apply the same exclusion in code but do not record the count, so their cells are blank rather than copied. The last column is the password-locking study's two families, which are its fine-tuning set and its held-out counterpart: every general experiment excludes them, the behaviour pass answers them so the lock study has replies to read, and nothing else touches them. Blocks and depths are where states were read or replaced; the atlas reads three depths and lists all three.}
